title: Applied LLM
blurb: Ship with models. This is the engineer half of Maxime Labonne’s LLM course, in watch order.

stages.title: Use one
stages.blurb: What a language model is, and a working practice, before any training.

stages.title: A chain
stages.blurb: LangChain, from the people who built it. The RAG series and LlamaIndex are on the App stack track.

stages.title: See the model
stages.blurb: Enough of the architecture to debug an application. Stop before you start pretraining.

stages.title: Ship an application
stages.blurb: Production, retrieval, evals, and running a model you can afford.

stages.title: Advanced
stages.blurb: The failure modes, the habits, and the point where your own model beats the API.

title: App stack
blurb: The basic application layer. Chains, retrieval, and a graph you can control. LangChain’s own tutorials, then LlamaIndex on documents.

stages.title: Chains
stages.blurb: Harrison Chase on context and LangSmith, then the expression language the library is built on.

stages.title: Retrieval
stages.blurb: What RAG is, derived, then LangChain’s own four-part tutorial: overview, index, retrieve, generate.

stages.title: A schema
stages.blurb: The model has to return a shape the rest of the program can trust. OpenAI’s own session on structured outputs.

stages.title: A graph
stages.blurb: The Anthropic agent patterns, implemented in LangGraph by the LangChain team.

stages.title: Documents
stages.blurb: Jerry Liu, LlamaIndex, on why a PDF is not a prompt.

title: LLM inference
blurb: From the cache and the kernel to vLLM, SGLang, and a model split across GPUs.

stages.title: KV cache
stages.blurb: Attention, then the cache that makes the next token cheap. LLaMA is where the cache, RoPE, and grouped-query attention show up together.

stages.title: The kernel and the bits
stages.blurb: FlashAttention from the author, the current kernel, then quantization so the weights fit.

stages.title: Serve one machine
stages.blurb: The CS336 inference lecture, PagedAttention, SGLang, then speculative decoding for the latency that is left.

stages.title: Several GPUs
stages.blurb: How a GPU runs the matmul, how tensor and pipeline parallelism split the model, then multi-GPU inference in vLLM.

title: Fine-tuning
blurb: Supervised finetuning, LoRA from the inventor, QLoRA from the author, then preference tuning.

stages.title: After pretraining
stages.blurb: What the post-training stage is, then supervised finetuning as a training procedure.

stages.title: Adapters
stages.blurb: The inventor of LoRA, the code, then Tim Dettmers on finetuning a quantized model.

stages.title: Preferences
stages.blurb: DPO derived, RLHF with the code, then what comes after DPO.

title: Architectures
blurb: The same decoder is not the same model. GPT-2, LLaMA, Mixtral, DeepSeek’s latent attention, and Kimi.

stages.title: GPT-2
stages.blurb: A dense decoder. The picture, then Karpathy building it, then a real 124M training run.

stages.title: LLaMA
stages.blurb: RoPE, RMSNorm, SwiGLU, grouped-query attention, and the KV cache. Explained, then coded.

stages.title: Mixture of experts
stages.blurb: CS336 on MoE as a systems choice, then Mistral’s sliding window and Mixtral’s sparse experts.

stages.title: DeepSeek and Kimi
stages.blurb: Multi-head latent attention, which is how DeepSeek shrinks the cache, then Zhilin Yang on how Moonshot scaled Kimi.

title: Vision-language
blurb: Image patches as tokens, a frozen language model that can see, then instruction tuning.

stages.title: Patches
stages.blurb: Lucas Beyer on transformers in vision, before the language model is attached.

stages.title: A language model that sees
stages.blurb: Flamingo, from an author. Few-shot visual tasks with a frozen language model.

stages.title: Instruction tuning
stages.blurb: Chunyuan Li on large multimodal models and the LLaVA line.

title: LLM researcher
blurb: Build the model. Intuition, then a small GPT, then Stanford CS336 in order. That course is the scientist path people mean.

stages.title: The mechanism
stages.blurb: Networks, gradients, backprop, then attention. Watch these before the code.

stages.title: Build a small one
stages.blurb: Karpathy’s Zero to Hero, the four lectures that end in a tokenizer.

stages.title: CS336, in order
stages.blurb: Language modeling from scratch. Do the assignments on the course site as you go.

stages.title: Train and align
stages.blurb: A real small training run, then preference tuning past the slogan.

stages.title: RLVR and environments
stages.blurb: A checker for a reward, the GRPO loss, then the environment the model is trained in. Nathan Lambert, then Prime Intellect.

title: Agentic engineer
blurb: How to build an agent, then the harness around it. The written tutorial is the Hugging Face agents course. The videos here are the ones worth watching.

stages.title: What an agent is
stages.blurb: The author of smolagents, then Anthropic on when an agent is worth building. Do the Hugging Face unit 1 notebook after the first video.

stages.title: Tutorials
stages.blurb: Short, official, at the keyboard. Follow along.

stages.title: How a lab runs them
stages.blurb: The practice once the demo works.

stages.title: Engineer the harness
stages.blurb: Context, tools, sandbox, the loop, and the receipt. In the order of the harness pack.
